newsitem.title: USA: GM says strike idles 50 more U.S. workers.
newsitem.headline: GM says strike idles 50 more U.S. workers.

text.p: General Motors Corp. said the strike against its Canadian operations forced it to idle 50 more workers Friday at its Ypsilanti, Mich., transmission plant.

GM said the total number of U.S. workers affected by the Canadian Auto Workers union's walkout remains relatively low, at 2,000. A total of 950 were idled at the Ypsilanti plant and an additional 1,050 at GM's North Tonawanda, N.Y., engine plant near Buffalo.
Analysts say GM has been able to handle the effects of the strike because it had ample warning that the CAW was preparing to strike, allowing it to build stockpiles of parts.
GM Canada spokesman D. Stewart Low declined to discuss the steps the automaker took to protect its U.S. operations from shutdown.
"We made contingency plans as part of our business plan if we encountered a work stoppage," he said.
GM's stock was up 50 cents at $50.375 in midday trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
